title: The focus ring is drawn in redline, the ink the colour lock reserves for a deviation
body:
## Summary
Every control on the Blocks sheet takes a redline focus ring, while the direction's colour lock reserves redline for a deviation from the specification; on a sheet whose subject is deviations, a focused control reads as a flagged one.

## Description
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/base/tokens.css:6-23 states the lock: redline for a deviation, greenline for a check that passed, gold for an unadjudicated pair and nothing else. examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/base/the-sheet.css:34-37 draws `.bk-root :where(button, select, input, a, [tabindex]):focus-visible` in `--bk-redline`. Two rules already depart from it on their own grounds: `.bk-l0-canvas:focus-visible` (level0/l0.css:54) and `.bk-cell:focus-visible` (level1/l1-cells.css) ring in graphite, and the title block now rings in the sheet's colour (2fe468b). So the sheet carries three focus inks and the one used most is the one the lock gives a different meaning. Fixed would be one focus ink, named in the lock's list (graphite on the stock, sheet on the inverted block, both well over 3:1), or the lock amended to name focus as redline's second use. Which is a design call on the law brief, not a contrast defect: redline clears 3:1 on both stock grounds (5.79 / 5.06:1).

## Flow
- Tab through the L0 legend keys of a database in fault: the key's redline verdict stripe and the redline focus ring are the same ink, side by side
- Tab to the dossier's Close or a spelling chip: the ring says 'deviation' around a control that deviates from nothing
- For the fix: pick the focus ink, add it to the lock's list in base/tokens.css, redraw the base ring, drop the two per-rule overrides that exist only because the base ring is red

## Expected impact
A reader scanning for red finds only deviations; keyboard focus stops competing with the verdict ink. Could break: the ring's salience on the vellum if graphite is chosen (13.17:1, still high).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one meaning per hue on a sheet whose whole read is hue-coded
Before: 1 base focus rule in redline over every control; 2 rules ring in graphite and 1 in sheet; the lock names redline for deviations only
After: one focus ink, listed in the lock
Method: simulation - the contrast is measured (both inks clear 3:1); whether the redline ring confuses a reader is a judgment on the law brief no gate can take
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

instrument: Playwright (or Chromium headless) with forcedColors: 'active' over the built page: computed style of a pressed vs an unpressed `.bk-seg-option`, a hovered/focused `.bk-cell`, and a fault vs quiet `.bk-db-key`; Before: pressed and unpressed paint identically; After: a structural carrier (outline, border width, text decoration) separates them
title: No forced-colors path: the pressed camera pose and other states carried by colour alone vanish
body:
## Summary
The Blocks sheet declares no `@media (forced-colors: active)` rule, and several states are carried only by a background or a border colour, which forced colours repaint to the system palette, so they disappear.

## Description
Under forced colours the platform replaces background-color, color and border-color with system colours. examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/level0/l0.css:180-183 draws the pressed camera pose (`.bk-seg-option[aria-pressed="true"]`) only as a graphite background with sheet text: repainted, the pressed pose looks like the other four. The legend key's verdict stripe (l0.css:214-220) is a border colour on an edge every key has at the same width, so fault and quiet read the same. `.bk-cell:hover/:focus-visible` (level1/l1-cells.css) changes only a border colour on a 1px border, which forced colours draws on every card. The registry's preference-respect technique: meaning survives the repaint only when a structural carrier (outline, width, icon, text) pairs the colour. The database jump already does it right (`.bk-db-jump[aria-pressed]` widens its inline-start border to 3px, level1/l1-grid.css). Fixed: a forced-colors block that gives each colour-only state a structural carrier, e.g. a 3px inline-start border on the pressed pose, a width difference on the fault stripe.

## Flow
- Windows High Contrast (or DevTools 'Emulate forced-colors: active') on the tidycrm page
- Press 'Front' among the camera poses: no pose reads as pressed
- The L0 legend: fault and quiet keys are indistinguishable (the seed has no quiet key, so only via a synthetic state)
- Build order: instrument (forced-colors emulation over the four states) -> CSS block in base/reduced-motion.css's neighbour or a new part imported last -> re-measure

## Expected impact
A forced-colours user can tell which camera pose is active and which databases are in fault. Could break: nothing outside forced-colours mode, if the block is scoped by the media query.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - colour-borne states survive a forced-colours repaint
Before: 0 `forced-colors` rules in the sheet (grep); 3 states whose only carrier is a colour (pressed pose, verdict stripe, card hover/focus)
After: each of the 3 has a structural carrier under forced colours
Method: simulation - the count is from the source; whether the repaint actually erases each state needs a browser with forced-colours emulation, which this round may not run
Result: better
Gate: none
